scenes.text: You keep all your gold in a wooden chest.
So you tie it shut with rope. They just cut it.
So you put a giant rock on top. They just push it off.
So you slide a wooden bolt across your door. Safe. But you can only lock it from the inside.
You need a lock that only you can open. So you drop little pins into the bolt, held down by springs. Now it is stuck.
Then you carve a key with bumps that lift every pin to exactly the right height. The gaps all line up, and it turns.
Wrong key? The pins stop at the wrong heights. Stuck.
Congratulations. You invented the pin tumbler lock.
The first ones were made of wood, in ancient Egypt, about four thousand years ago. And the same idea is in almost every front door today.
